pages.intent: the quarter's headline results and how they landed against guidance
pages.message: Revenue grew 21.3% to $358.2M and non-GAAP operating margin widened 5.4 points to 16.6%, both above the top of guidance

exhibits.reader_must_see: the six headline metrics of the quarter, each with its change on the year before, at a glance
exhibits.comparison: each Q3 FY26 metric against Q3 FY25
exhibits.data: six single figures in mixed units (dollars, percent, points), each with a year-on-year change

forms_considered.form: row of headline metric tiles
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the investor-relations convention; the figure is large and its growth sits under it

forms_considered.form: one summary table of metrics
forms_considered.reason: holds the figures but gives the headline no more weight than the detail below it

forms_considered.form: six small sparkline charts
forms_considered.reason: nine-quarter trends belong on the next pages; here the reader wants the number

exhibits.why: the analyst's first question is the headline number and its growth; tiles on one pale ground give six figures equal weight and read in seconds
exhibits.marks: each figure in indigo, the current quarter; its change on the year before in the caption under it; the record net new ARR named in its tile

exhibits.reader_must_see: that each headline metric got here by a steady climb, the current quarter the latest step
exhibits.comparison: each metric's current quarter against its own previous eight quarters
exhibits.data: six series of nine quarterly values, one per headline metric

forms_considered.form: small column sparkline in each tile, first and last values labelled
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the shape of nine quarters under the figure, with the current bar in indigo and its two end values stated

forms_considered.form: a separate nine-quarter table
forms_considered.reason: repeats pages 2 to 4 in figures; the reader here needs the direction and its two ends, not every value

forms_considered.form: no trend on the summary page
forms_considered.reason: a figure without its history invites the question whether it is a blip

exhibits.chosen_form: small column sparkline in each tile, first and last values labelled
exhibits.why: a tile states the figure; the sparkline under it answers whether it is a trend, its first and last labels say how far it came, and every value lives on the later pages
exhibits.marks: the Q3 FY26 bar and its label in indigo, earlier bars in slate; retention drawn as an indigo line labelled at its start, trough and end; a caption under the tiles says what the bars span

exhibits.reader_must_see: the supporting metrics behind the headline: backlog, large customers, GAAP margin and stock compensation, against last year
exhibits.comparison: each metric in Q3 FY26 against Q3 FY25, with the change
exhibits.data: six metrics by two quarters and a change column, mixed units

forms_considered.form: two-period metrics table with a change column
forms_considered.reason: chosen: reads across a row, last year to this year to the change

forms_considered.form: more headline tiles
forms_considered.reason: a second row of tiles would flatten the hierarchy and crowd the page

exhibits.chosen_form: two-period metrics table with a change column
exhibits.why: these are figures to look up and check, which a table serves, and the change column carries the comparison
exhibits.marks: the Q3 FY26 column in indigo; nothing worsened, so no red

exhibits.reader_must_see: that revenue and operating income both landed above the top of the range guided in August
exhibits.comparison: each actual against the guided low and high given in August, and the beat against the high end
exhibits.data: three metrics, each a guided low, a guided high and an actual

forms_considered.form: guidance scorecard table
forms_considered.reason: chosen: guided range, actual and beat read in one row for each metric

forms_considered.form: floating range bars with an actual marker
forms_considered.reason: three metrics on three scales need three charts for three rows of figures

exhibits.why: an analyst checks the beat against the stated range, a figure to quote; the table gives it directly
exhibits.marks: the guided range in grey, superseded by the actual; each beat in green

exhibits.reader_must_see: that full-year guidance went up with the quarter
exhibits.comparison: the FY2026 range issued in October against the range guided in August
exhibits.data: three metrics, each a range now and a range in August

forms_considered.form: two-column guidance table, now against August
forms_considered.reason: chosen: each row reads the new range against the one it replaces

forms_considered.form: a sentence in the notes column
forms_considered.reason: a range of the form 1,394.4-1,398.4 breaks at its hyphen in a narrow column, and the August range would need a second sentence

forms_considered.form: floating range bars by update
forms_considered.reason: page 5 draws every update; here the reader needs the latest change

exhibits.chosen_form: two-column guidance table, now against August
exhibits.why: the raise is a figure analysts quote; a table states both ranges and puts the full outlook on page 5
exhibits.marks: the new guidance in amber, the colour of guidance in force; August's in grey, as on page 5

pages.intent: nine quarters of revenue and ARR growth
pages.message: ARR grew 22.2% to $1,498M on a record $83M of net new ARR, while revenue growth held at 21.3-21.7% for five quarters

exhibits.reader_must_see: revenue rising every quarter and its growth rate settling at 21-22% after FY2024's 23-27%
exhibits.comparison: each quarter's revenue against the quarters before it, and its growth against the year before
exhibits.data: total revenue by nine quarters, with a year-on-year growth rate per quarter

forms_considered.form: labelled columns with a growth row under the quarters
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the level and its growth read in the same column

forms_considered.form: columns on one axis and a growth line on a second axis
forms_considered.reason: two scales invite reading the line against the bars, a false comparison

forms_considered.form: stacked subscription and services columns
forms_considered.reason: services are 4% of revenue and would be slivers; one colour per series would cost the current-quarter meaning

exhibits.chosen_form: labelled columns with a growth row under the quarters
exhibits.why: investors read revenue level and growth together; a row of growth figures under each column keeps the growth exact without a second axis
exhibits.marks: Q3 FY26 in indigo, prior quarters in slate; growth figures in a row under the quarters

exhibits.reader_must_see: net new ARR at a record $83M in Q3 FY26 and the ending ARR it built
exhibits.comparison: each quarter's net new ARR against every earlier quarter, and ending ARR quarter by quarter
exhibits.data: net new ARR by nine quarters, with ending ARR and its growth per quarter

forms_considered.form: net new ARR columns with an ending-ARR row under the quarters
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the record is the tallest column and the stock it builds reads beneath

forms_considered.form: ending ARR columns
forms_considered.reason: the stock rises smoothly and hides the record quarter, which is a flow

forms_considered.form: a table of ARR and net new ARR
forms_considered.reason: carries the figures but the reader must hunt for the record

exhibits.chosen_form: net new ARR columns with an ending-ARR row under the quarters
exhibits.why: the claim is the record flow; columns of the flow make it the tallest mark, and the ending ARR stays exact in the row
exhibits.marks: the Q3 FY26 column in indigo with its label reading record; ending ARR and its growth in rows under the quarters

exhibits.reader_must_see: that subscription revenue is nearly all of revenue and grew faster than the total
exhibits.comparison: subscription against services, Q3 FY26 against Q3 FY25
exhibits.data: two revenue lines and their total by two quarters with growth rates

forms_considered.form: small revenue-by-type table with a totals row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the split, the growth and a total that ties

forms_considered.form: stacked columns of subscription and services
forms_considered.reason: services at 4% would be a sliver too thin to label

exhibits.chosen_form: small revenue-by-type table with a totals row
exhibits.why: the reader checks the mix as figures; a three-row table ties to the revenue chart beside it
exhibits.marks: the Q3 FY26 column in indigo; the total bold under a rule

exhibits.reader_must_see: that ARR growth has just moved ahead of revenue growth after five quarters behind it, the lead indicator turning first
exhibits.comparison: ARR growth against revenue growth, quarter by quarter over nine quarters
exhibits.data: two growth rates in percent over nine quarters, close together and crossing three times

forms_considered.form: two growth lines on one axis
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the crossing and the gap between the two rates read as one picture

forms_considered.form: a growth-gap column per quarter
forms_considered.reason: shows the gap but hides each rate, which the notes beside it quote

forms_considered.form: no growth chart beside the notes
forms_considered.reason: the claim that ARR now leads would rest on two category rows read side by side

exhibits.chosen_form: two growth lines on one axis
exhibits.why: the reader asks whether faster ARR growth will carry revenue growth with it; two lines show where ARR fell behind and where it crossed back
exhibits.marks: ARR in indigo and revenue in slate, each labelled at its first and last quarter; the caption names the crossing

pages.intent: retention, cohort expansion and the cost of growth
pages.message: Net revenue retention rose for a third quarter to 119% and the FY2024 cohort expanded 1.47x in its second year, the fastest of any cohort

exhibits.reader_must_see: net revenue retention bottoming at 116% and rising three points to 119%, with gross retention steady at 92-94% beneath
exhibits.comparison: each quarter's retention against the quarters before it, net against gross

forms_considered.form: net retention line with gross retention as a row of figures beneath
forms_considered.reason: chosen: net retention on its own tight scale shows the trough and turn; gross retention, nearly flat, reads as figures

forms_considered.form: two labelled lines on one scale
forms_considered.reason: a scale wide enough for both flattens net retention's three-point turn

forms_considered.form: clustered columns of net and gross retention
forms_considered.reason: eighteen columns near 100% would differ by slivers

exhibits.chosen_form: net retention line with gross retention as a row of figures beneath
exhibits.why: retention is a rate whose turn is the claim; a line shows the trough and the recovery, and labels keep each value exact
exhibits.marks: net retention in indigo with every value labelled and the 116% trough labelled low; gross retention as a row of figures under the quarters

exhibits.reader_must_see: every annual cohort expanding its ARR, and the FY2024 cohort ahead of the others at the same age
exhibits.comparison: each cohort's ARR multiple against the other cohorts at the same years since landing
exhibits.data: five annual cohorts by up to five years since landing, an ARR multiple of the first year, a triangle

forms_considered.form: one line per cohort over years since landing
forms_considered.reason: chosen: cohorts at the same age line up vertically and the faster one sits above

forms_considered.form: a triangle table of multiples
forms_considered.reason: exact but the reader compares numbers down a column to find the fastest

forms_considered.form: a stacked layer-cake area of ARR by cohort
forms_considered.reason: shows the stock by vintage but not the expansion rate the claim is about

exhibits.chosen_form: one line per cohort over years since landing
exhibits.why: aligning cohorts by age makes faster expansion visible as a higher line; the claim is a comparison at the same age
exhibits.marks: the FY2024 cohort in indigo, others in slate; each line named with its latest multiple at its end

exhibits.reader_must_see: the cost of growth improving: payback shorter and the ARR magic number higher in Q3 FY26
exhibits.comparison: each unit-economics metric over five quarters
exhibits.data: six metrics by five quarters, mixed units (percent, months, multiple, count)

forms_considered.form: five-quarter metrics table
forms_considered.reason: chosen: six metrics in mixed units read across five quarters

forms_considered.form: small multiple column charts
forms_considered.reason: six charts in a third of a page would be too small to label

exhibits.why: mixed units resist one chart; an analyst copies these figures into a model, and a table gives them exactly
exhibits.marks: the Q3 FY26 column in indigo; payback and magic number rows bold, the two the page states

pages.intent: where the year's operating margin expansion came from and how GAAP reconciles
pages.message: Non-GAAP operating margin widened 5.4 points to 16.6%, 3.1 of them from sales and marketing; GAAP operating loss narrowed to $1.3M

exhibits.reader_must_see: the 5.4-point widening split into its four cost lines, with sales and marketing the largest step
exhibits.comparison: each cost line's contribution against the others, from Q3 FY25 margin to Q3 FY26 margin
exhibits.data: a start margin, four signed steps in points of revenue and an end margin

forms_considered.form: margin bridge in points of revenue
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the steps add visibly from one margin to the other

forms_considered.form: table of cost ratios by year
forms_considered.reason: carries the ratios but the reader subtracts to find the drivers

forms_considered.form: stacked columns of cost structure for two quarters
forms_considered.reason: the changes are under four points and vanish in a 100% stack

exhibits.chosen_form: margin bridge in points of revenue
exhibits.why: the question is what moved the margin; a bridge sizes each driver and ties to both margins
exhibits.marks: start in slate, end in indigo, each widening step in green with its signed value above it; the sales and marketing step labelled with its 57% share of the gain

exhibits.reader_must_see: the cost ratios behind the bridge for each of the last five quarters
exhibits.comparison: each cost line as a share of revenue quarter by quarter
exhibits.data: five ratios by five quarters, percent of revenue

forms_considered.form: five-quarter cost structure table
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the reader recomputes the bridge from the first and last columns

forms_considered.form: line chart of each ratio
forms_considered.reason: four lines on one scale from 8% to 80% flatten every change

exhibits.why: the bridge needs its inputs where an analyst can check them; the table supplies them
exhibits.marks: the operating margin row bold; the Q3 FY26 column in indigo

exhibits.reader_must_see: how GAAP operating loss reconciles to non-GAAP operating income in each quarter, and that it narrowed to $1.3M
exhibits.comparison: each adjustment against the others and GAAP against non-GAAP, quarter by quarter
exhibits.data: a GAAP figure, four adjustments and a non-GAAP total by five quarters, in dollars

forms_considered.form: reconciliation table with a totals row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the required disclosure form, and the totals tie

forms_considered.form: a GAAP to non-GAAP bridge chart
forms_considered.reason: a second bridge on the page, in dollars, would compete with the margin bridge

exhibits.chosen_form: reconciliation table with a totals row
exhibits.why: investors expect the reconciliation as a table that ties; it is checked figure by figure
exhibits.marks: the non-GAAP total bold under a rule; the Q3 FY26 column in indigo

exhibits.reader_must_see: operating cash flow less capital expenditure giving free cash flow in each of the five quarters
exhibits.comparison: free cash flow quarter by quarter, and against the operating cash flow behind it
exhibits.data: operating cash flow, capital expenditure and free cash flow by five quarters, in dollars

forms_considered.form: three-line cash flow table with a totals row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the free cash flow figure ties to its two inputs in each quarter

forms_considered.form: columns of free cash flow
forms_considered.reason: drops the inputs an analyst checks and adds a third chart form to the page

exhibits.chosen_form: three-line cash flow table with a totals row
exhibits.why: free cash flow is the figure under the margin; a table that ties shows it is real cash
exhibits.marks: free cash flow bold under a rule; the Q3 FY26 column in indigo

pages.intent: the outlook for Q4 and the full year
pages.message: FY2026 revenue guidance raised for a third time, to $1,394.4-1,398.4M or 20.9-21.3% growth, $36.4M above the initial midpoint

exhibits.reader_must_see: the Q4 FY26 and FY2026 guidance ranges for revenue, growth, operating income and margin, beside the prior FY2026 guidance
exhibits.comparison: the new full-year range against the range given in August, and each guided figure against the year before
exhibits.data: four metrics by three guidance columns (Q4, FY2026 now, FY2026 prior), each a low to high range

forms_considered.form: guidance table of ranges
forms_considered.reason: chosen: ranges are quoted as text and modelled as figures

forms_considered.form: range bars per metric
forms_considered.reason: four metrics in four units each need their own scale

exhibits.why: guidance is what analysts copy into the model; the table gives the ranges exactly and the prior guidance beside them
exhibits.marks: the new guidance columns in amber, the forward-looking colour; the prior guidance column muted

exhibits.reader_must_see: the FY2026 revenue range moving up at each of the four updates, the latest highest
exhibits.comparison: each guidance range against the ones before it on one dollar scale
exhibits.data: four low and high revenue ranges for one fiscal year, with their midpoints

forms_considered.form: floating horizontal range bars on one dollar axis
forms_considered.reason: chosen: each update's range is a bar and the move up reads left to right

forms_considered.form: column chart of guidance midpoints
forms_considered.reason: drops the width of each range, which narrowed as the year closed

forms_considered.form: a table of the four ranges
forms_considered.reason: exact but the reader must subtract to see the raises

exhibits.chosen_form: floating horizontal range bars on one dollar axis
exhibits.why: the claim is a sequence of raises; ranges on one axis show both the step up and the narrowing
exhibits.marks: the current range in amber, superseded ranges in slate; low and high at the bar ends; the initial and current midpoints as text with the $36.4M raise

exhibits.reader_must_see: how far each cost line and margin still sits from the long-term target model
exhibits.comparison: each line's Q3 FY26 share of revenue against its target range
exhibits.data: six ratios, each a current value and a target range

forms_considered.form: two-column target model table
forms_considered.reason: chosen: current figure beside the target range, the way target models are published

forms_considered.form: bullet bars of current against target
forms_considered.reason: six bars in a narrow column would be too small to label

exhibits.why: targets are quoted ranges; a table keeps them exact and leaves the gap to the reader
exhibits.marks: targets in amber, the forward-looking colour; the current column in indigo; the operating margin gap stated in a note
